question: Can a visibly non-sequential transition grammar communicate that the user has entered a different already-ready context, while remaining recognizably compatible with Kymaean and avoiding false process, priority, causal, navigation-direction, or Stage semantics?

definitions.context_shift: A transition between two already-available information/identity contexts where the organizing frame or mode materially changes. It is not loading, task completion, provider response, route progress, live data arrival, Character action, Scene/Stage change, Performance, Take, Opportunity, or any transcript-dependent event.
definitions.within_context_succession: A bounded 2–4-unit eligible succession inside one established context; this remains F1A territory.
definitions.ownership: A context shift owns its transition boundary. F1A may not execute concurrently with, or automatically chain immediately after, the context-shift treatment for the same event.

fixed_laws.f1a_unchanged: 70 ms onset / 460 ms equal movement / cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); not under test here.
fixed_laws.reduced_motion: Immediate final context, zero transition animation, no information/function loss.

neutral_comparison.content: Two neutral already-ready fields named Context A and Context B with equivalent information density; no Kymaean/Ensemble naming, marks, palette/material identity, imagery, product-state labels, Stage semantics, loading/progress language, or directional navigation labels.

control.name: Immediate Cut
control.mechanism: Outgoing field removed and incoming field rendered synchronously with no animation.
control.role: No-motion baseline; not a candidate identity treatment.

candidates.name: Synchronized Field Settle
candidates.mechanism: The incoming field moves as one synchronized block through a shallow single-axis translation; no per-element delay and no outgoing-field choreography.
candidates.risk_to_test: May feel like a generic panel entrance or imply spatial navigation if displacement is too strong.

candidates.name: Balanced Crossfade Exchange
candidates.mechanism: Outgoing and incoming fields exchange opacity simultaneously around the same fixed geometry; no per-element timing differences and no implied directional travel.
candidates.risk_to_test: May be too generic or visually weak to register as a deliberate Kymaean context change.

candidates.name: Simultaneous Opposed-Field Exchange
candidates.mechanism: Outgoing and incoming fields translate simultaneously in opposite vertical directions with equal timing; every element within each field moves together.
candidates.risk_to_test: May imply previous/next or spatial navigation despite neutral content.

fixture_only_ranges.duration_ms: 240–340 candidate comparison range; exact specimen values must be frozen before execution and carry no production-token authority.
fixture_only_ranges.crossfade_opacity: 0 to 1 only for CS2; no semantic content may disappear under reduced motion.

preflight: Exact candidate/control matrix membership across APP/WEB × WIDE/320.
No stagger or element-level timing differences in CS1-CS3.
Final visual/information state is equivalent across full and reduced motion.
Forced reduced motion produces zero transition animations.
No candidate exposes loading/progress/priority/causal/Stage/navigation-direction semantics in text or structure.

questions: Does the treatment read as a genuine change of context rather than succession within one context?
Is it clearly different from F1A Ordered Stagger?
Does it avoid implying loading, process, priority, causality, back/forward navigation, or Stage semantics?
Does it remain restrained enough for APP while retaining deliberate character on WEB?
Is the no-motion cut preferable to any candidate?
adjudication.outcomes: Select at most one provisional context-shift treatment, or select CUT/none if no animated candidate earns the role. No evidence-aware retune inside the same comparison after viewing.

next_action: Freeze exact fixture timings/amplitudes, materialize CS0-CS3 neutral APP/WEB × WIDE/320 comparison, run full/reduced-motion browser preflight, freeze Design Sol view, then present to Director.
